correctness.rationale: Direct expansion with u=g/||g|| and v=(-u2,u1) gives the PSD rank-one residual ab vv^T/(a u1²+b u2²), whose Frobenius norm is its sole nonzero eigenvalue. The optimum Frobenius tail is b, so R=κ/[1+(κ−1)T] with T=u1². The Gaussian direction is uniform on the circle, T has the arcsine density, and inversion gives the claimed CDF (at κ=1 the law is a point mass). The first two angular integrals follow from tan θ substitution and differentiation in the two denominator coefficients. For q<1/2, t^(−q) is an integrable majorant against the arcsine law; for q>1/2, scaling t=s/κ on t≤1/2 gives the stated beta constant and the upper half contributes O(1). For q=1/2, the integral is (2/π)K(1−1/κ) in parameter convention, with endpoint log(4√κ)+o(1) for K, giving coefficient 1/π and bounded remainder. For any unit isotropic probe E[T]=1/2; strict Jensen gives equality precisely at constant squared coordinate energies, and the normalized independent signs attain it with zero cross moment. The statement is about a fixed known eigenbasis, not uniform benefit over unknown rotations.
